subject: Proposed High-Availability Addendum & Order Form Clauses — execution timeline
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@astracrest.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: high-availability addendum + order form clauses

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and engineering asked me to reach out with a small set of asks so we can close the procurement review for our enterprise MSA/SOW. High level: AstraCrest needs a tailored availability addendum that spells out uptime/latency commitments for our primary EU/US workloads, an order-form appendix with the credit schedule, and a short evidence checklist (telemetry, retention, audit hooks) for our compliance team.

Questions we need answered before legal will circulate the final redlines:
- Proposed uptime target (monthly) and the credit schedule for breaches
- Latency SLOs for API tails (95th/99th) and whether Redwood will support a guaranteed 95th < 200ms for small inference requests
- What fallback model/region behavior is covered under the addendum during partial outages
- Telemetry evidence we can request during audits (sample queries, retention windows)

Can you send a draft addendum + suggested order-form language we can share with our legal and SRE teams? We are hoping to get this into DocuSign by the end of next week (target 5/28).

Attaching the MSA and SOW excerpts we referenced in the call (see attached).

Appreciate any clarity you can provide — happy to set a 30m call if easier.

Best,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Sr. Procurement Manager | AstraCrest Labs
attachments: AstraCrest_MSA_excerpt.pdf (pdf), AstraCrest_SOW_excerpt.pdf (pdf)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@astracrest.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: high-availability addendum + order form clauses

Alex —

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. I attached a first-pass draft addendum (Redwood_HA_Addendum_v1.docx), a short text file with suggested order-form clause language, and an evidence checklist for your compliance team. Highlights in plain language:

- Monthly uptime target: 99.95% (regional), with a graduated credit schedule: 99.95–99.80: 10% credit; 99.79–99.00: 25% credit; <99.00: 50% credit.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile < 180ms, 99th percentile < 450ms for single-request text generation (payloads < 512 tokens). We can tighten the 95th to 160ms on Dedicated pools — noted in the doc.
- Fallbacks: we define automatic regional failover and model-variant fallback behavior; fallbacks will not count as availability if capacity constraints are caused by customer-specific dedicated capacity (we call that out).
- Evidence: we provide 90 days of request-level telemetry, 12 months of aggregated SLO/incident reports, and an audit-runbook bundle on request (see Evidence_Checklist_Redwood.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik and Ben to review for procurement/ops wording and send redlines by EOD 5/24.
2) We schedule a 30m alignment call 5/25 (I can do 10:00–13:00 PT).
3) If AstraCrest legal is good with content, we’ll push a prefilled DocuSign packet 5/26 so it can circulate internally for signature the week of 5/27.

If that timeline works for you, I’ll loop in our legal ops contact and produce the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Enterprise Contracts | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for pulling the team in. Procurement reviewed the language and legal had two minor asks: include an example credit calculation in the addendum (so it is explicit how credits are applied to monthly invoices) and permit a single audit request per 12-month period (we'll include a 30-day notice).
